nphi.title: Five-nation public health institute exchanges on data sharing, digitalisation and AI
nphi.with: US CDC; Australian CDC; Public Health Agency of Canada; New Zealand public health agency
nphi.summary: UKHSA held regular meetings in 2024/25 with the public health institutes of the US, Australia, Canada and New Zealand on data sharing, digitalisation and artificial intelligence.

nphi.title: PHF Science – Kiribati Ministry of Health MoU
nphi.with: Kiribati Ministry of Health and Medical Services; Kiribati Police Service
nphi.summary: MoU signed in February 2024 laying the basis for joint research on AMR, water quality and the combined burden of communicable and non-communicable disease, plus training and knowledge transfer for Kiribati health and police staff.

nphi.title: APCOVE – Asia Pacific Consortium of Veterinary Epidemiology (phases 1 and 2)
nphi.with: Australian and New Zealand veterinary schools; national animal health services
nphi.summary: DFAT-funded consortium set up in 2020 to build veterinary epidemiology capacity for animal and zoonotic disease surveillance in eight Asia-Pacific countries.

nphi.title: SHIVERS – Southern Hemisphere Influenza and Vaccine Effectiveness Research and Surveillance
nphi.with: St. Jude Center of Excellence for Influenza Research and Surveillance; US NIAID; Universities of Auckland and Otago
nphi.summary: Long-running influenza research and surveillance programme led by ESR with US partners; SHIVERS-II (2018), funded by NIAID through St. Jude, followed a Wellington cohort to study immune responses to infection and vaccination.

nphi.title: Pacific Public Health Surveillance Network (PPHSN) – LabNet, EpiNet, PacNet, PICNet
nphi.actor: Pacific Community (SPC) – Pacific Public Health Surveillance Network (PPHSN)
nphi.with: Health ministries of Pacific Island countries and territories; WHO; US CDC; ESR/PHF Science; Fiji National University; PIHOA; regional reference laboratories
nphi.summary: Regional surveillance network set up in 1996 under SPC and WHO, with a three-tier laboratory network (regional level-2 labs in Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam and New Caledonia; reference labs in Australia, New Zealand and the US), outbreak…

nphi.title: FNU Communicable Diseases Research Centre with University of Otago support
nphi.actor: Fiji National University (College of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences)
nphi.with: University of Otago Global Health Institute; Mercy Hospital Dunedin
nphi.summary: Communicable Diseases Research Centre set up in 2021 within FNU's Fiji Institute of Pacific Health Research, backed by Otago's Global Health Institute under a 2017 MoU and a funded research fellow post.

nphi.title: ESR COVID-19 testing and quality assurance for Pacific Island countries
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: WHO; Pacific Paramedical Training Centre; 24 Pacific laboratories
nphi.summary: Under a 2020 NZ Government agreement, ESR tested SARS-CoV-2 samples from Pacific countries lacking in-country capacity and extended its external quality assurance programme to 24 Pacific labs.

nphi.title: Enteric viruses in wastewater, seawater and shellfish in French Polynesia
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: French Polynesia: CHSP, DRMM, CRIOBE, CHPf; LIST; French Pacific Fund
nphi.summary: ESR and French Pacific Fund co-funded monitoring of enteric viruses in wastewater, seawater and shellfish in French Polynesia, started in 2015.

nphi.title: Strengthening water security of vulnerable island states
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: SPC Geoscience Division; NZ MFAT; Cook Islands; Tokelau
nphi.summary: MFAT-funded assessments in 2014–2015 with SPC of drinking-water availability, reliability and quality in isolated communities in five small Pacific island states.

nphi.title: Healthy Tonga Tourism
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: Tonga Ministry of Health; Tonga tourism ministry; NZ Aid Programme
nphi.summary: Three-year project from 2012 producing public health guidelines for tourist accommodation in Tonga on rainwater, food safety and mosquito-borne disease.

nphi.title: Enteric virus and norovirus monitoring in New Caledonia
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: DASS-NC; Institut Pasteur de Nouméa; Province Nord; French Pacific Fund
nphi.summary: Co-funded study started in 2011 with New Caledonia's health directorate and Institut Pasteur de Nouméa, the first monitoring of norovirus and other enteric viruses in people and waters there.

nphi.title: Lab-based influenza surveillance in Pacific Island countries (PPHSN)
nphi.actor: Institut Pasteur de Nouvelle-Calédonie (with Pacific Community)
nphi.with: Pacific Community (SPC); WHO National Influenza Centre at ESR; WHO CC for Influenza Melbourne; US CDC; Cook Islands, Guam, Wallis and Futuna
nphi.summary: US CDC-funded project from 2006 to set up laboratory-based influenza surveillance in Pacific Island countries, with confirmatory PCR at Institut Pasteur de Nouvelle-Calédonie and training at ESR and the Melbourne WHO collaborating centre.

nphi.title: Drinking-water safety planning training and policy support in the Pacific (WHO/SOPAC)
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: WHO South Pacific; SPC-SOPAC; DASS-NC; Cook Islands
nphi.summary: ESR delivered drinking-water safety planning workshops for Pacific countries from 2006 and helped draft Fiji's national drinking water safety plan for rural and island communities under WHO–SOPAC contracts.

nphi.title: WHO National Influenza Centre support to Pacific laboratories
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: SPC; WHO; Cook Islands, Guam, Niue, Tokelau, Wallis and Futuna, American Samoa
nphi.summary: As WHO National Influenza Centre, ESR provided influenza laboratory training, reference testing and sentinel surveillance support to Pacific island laboratories in 2006, 2009 and 2010.

nphi.title: PaNDAS – Pacific Networked Diagnostics and Support
nphi.actor: CSIRO Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness (ACDP)
nphi.with: Australian and New Zealand reference laboratories; Pacific veterinary laboratories
nphi.summary: ACDP-led project to establish a Pacific Laboratory Network that standardises diagnostics and supports animal and zoonotic disease investigations in Pacific island countries.

nphi.title: Healthy Tonga Environments – environmental health laboratory
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: Tonga Ministry of Health Environmental Health team; Vaiola Hospital laboratory
nphi.summary: ESR, with NZ Aid funding, helped set up an environmental health lab in Tonga (opened December 2019) for drinking-water quality monitoring and mosquito-borne disease prevention.

nphi.title: ESR–EWBNZ drinking water safety planning in Vanuatu
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: Department of Water Resources Vanuatu; Shefa Provincial Water Office; Engineers Without Borders NZ
nphi.summary: ESR supports Vanuatu's Department of Water Resources in rolling out Drinking Water Safety and Security Plans toward universal safe drinking water by 2030.

nphi.title: Healthy Water, Healthy People – Bitokara (PNG)
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: Caritas Aotearoa NZ; Catholic Diocese of Kimbe
nphi.summary: ESR WASH project providing rainwater harvesting and sanitation for about 1,700 people, a clinic and schools in West New Britain, PNG.

nphi.title: WASH in schools – Kiribati and Solomon Islands (SIBLE)
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.summary: MFAT-funded work with UNICEF NZ on school water, sanitation and hygiene toolkits, standards and safety planning for outer-island schools in Kiribati and Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands.
